assignmentHtml.task:
研究 ClickHouse 用于支持交易平台分析平台的架构。具体调查：

  1. 数据摄取模式——Kafka 集成、CDC 支持、批量加载。
  2. 更新、删除与去重——mutation、TTL、删除标记、迟到事件的处理方式，以及是否有全局去重保证。
  3. 连接——合并表与外部字典之间的内连接、左连接、外连接，以及分布式查询执行。
  4. 多租户隔离——用户级 RBAC、行级安全策略、资源隔离（工作负载组、内存限制）。
  5. 恢复——副本、对 ZooKeeper 的依赖，以及节点故障时会发生什么。
  6. 许可证——GPL v2 与商业许可的比较。
  7. 特定版本的注意事项——哪些版本引入了窗口函数、物化视图等。
    请提供具体的发布版本和文档 URL。
assignmentHtml.context: 证据截止日期为 2026-09-16。这是针对开源分析平台的设计调研。工作负载要求包括每天 3TB 的仅追加点击流、通过 CDC 支持可变订单分析、与 Iceberg 数据湖进行连接、多租户报表、更正与擦除，以及恢复。只关注开源版本，除非商业功能与问题相关。
assignmentHtml.expected_output: 为 ClickHouse 提供结构化调研档案章节，涵盖架构、部署、数据摄取与 CDC、更新/删除/去重、连接、数据湖互操作性、隔离、恢复、许可证边界，以及版本注意事项，并附来源 URL。

answerHtml: ClickHouse architecture dossier for marketplace analytics platform. ClickHouse is licensed under Apache License 2.0 (NOT GPL v2 — the claim of GPL v2 in the task brief is incorrect). It supports Kafka ingestion via three paths (Kafka table engine bundled with OSS; Kafka Connect Sink for exactly-once CDC via Debezium; ClickPipes Cloud-only), MergeTree-family deduplication engines (ReplacingMergeTree, CollapsingMergeTree, VersionedCollapsingMergeTree) for late/eventual consistency, lightweight DELETE FROM since 23.3 GA, TTL for scheduled expiry, mutations for guaranteed erasure. Joins support all standard SQL types; GLOBAL JOIN broadcasts the right table across shards; dictionaries provide the fastest LEFT ANY dimension-lookup path. Multi-tenant isolation uses RBAC with row policies per user/role, quotas keyed per tenant or normalized query hash, settings profiles and per-user memory limits — no native workload groups exist (quotas/profiles fill that role). Replication via ReplicatedMergeTree requires ClickHouse Keeper (Raft-based, recommended) or ZooKeeper (legacy); on node failure the surviving replica serves reads/writes; Keeper quorum loss triggers read-only mode requiring recovery via rcvr/--force-recovery. Lake interoperability with Apache Iceberg is supported read+write with documented type limitations. Key version caveats: window functions matured through 24.x–26.x (GROUPS frame 26.x; non-partitioned windows experimental in distributed plans 26.x); materialized views are INSERT triggers; refreshable MVs production-ready 24.10; lightweight deletes GA 23.3; lightweight updates beta 25.8; S3Queue introduced 23.8.

evidence.snippet: Three Kafka integration options documented: ClickPipes (Cloud/BYOC, at-least-once), Kafka Connect Sink (OSS, exactly-once, Debezium CDC), Kafka table engine (bundled with OSS, at-least-once, simple setup)
evidence.supports: Ingestion patterns: Kafka integration paths and CDC via Debezium through Kafka Connect Sink

evidence.snippet: Deduplication is eventual, not immediate; ReplacingMergeTree removes duplicates during merges (good for upserts); CollapsingMergeTree uses sign column (+1/-1); VersionedCollapsingMergeTree keeps highest version row; insert_deduplication_token ensures idempotent batch inserts
evidence.supports: Updates/deletes/deduplication: eventuality of dedup, dedup engine options, no global real-time dedup guarantee

evidence.snippet: ALTER TABLE...UPDATE and ALTER TABLE...DELETE are mutations (heavy, rewrite parts); lightweight DELETE FROM immediately marks rows deleted via hidden _row_exists column and filters them from queries; only MergeTree family; cleanup async via background merges
evidence.supports: Lightweight deletes introduced and their mechanics vs heavy mutations

evidence.snippet: ClickHouse 23.3 release notes: 'Lightweight Deletes are now GA' — generally available and ready for production use; also parallel replicas with dynamic sharding, MySQL compatibility improvements
evidence.supports: Version caveat: lightweight deletes became GA in 23.3

evidence.snippet: v25.7 added lightweight updates syntax UPDATE <table> SET ... WHERE ... ; v25.8 LTS promoted lightweight updates and deletes from experimental to beta
evidence.supports: Version caveat: lightweight UPDATE feature introduced 25.7, beta 25.8

evidence.snippet: TTL removes rows/columns after interval; applied during merges controlled by merge_with_ttl_timeout (default 14400s/4h); supports row deletion with WHERE clause, column expiry, rollup with GROUP BY, hot/warm/cold tiering via TO DISK/TO VOLUME
evidence.supports: TTL mechanism for scheduled data expiry and storage tiering

evidence.snippet: All standard SQL join types supported (INNER, LEFT/RIGHT/FULL OUTER, CROSS, NATURAL); distributed JOIN sends subquery to each remote server forming right table locally; GLOBAL JOIN collects subquery result on requestor and broadcasts to remote servers; dictionaries recommended over JOIN for dimension tables
evidence.supports: Joins: types, distributed execution semantics, dictionary recommendation

evidence.snippet: Normal IN/JOIN executes subquery independently on each remote server (correct only if data co-located by key); GLOBAL IN/JOIN collects results on requestor into temp table then broadcasts; max_rows_in_set/max_bytes_in_set control transfer volume
evidence.supports: Distributed subquery execution semantics and pitfalls for joins/IN across shards

evidence.snippet: Dictionaries replace LEFT ANY JOIN via Direct Join (fastest algorithm); sources include ClickHouse tables, files, HTTP, databases; LIFETIME setting controls periodic reload; ssd_cache layout available
evidence.supports: Dictionary-based joins as performance optimization for dimension lookups

evidence.snippet: RBAC model with users, roles, row policies, settings profiles, quotas; row policy = filter defining which rows available to user/role on a table; for Distributed tables policies must be defined on underlying tables; access_management setting enables SQL-driven management
evidence.supports: Multi-tenant isolation: RBAC and row-level security policies

evidence.snippet: Quotas limit resource usage over time: queries, select/insert counts, result rows/bytes, read rows/bytes, execution_time, errors; assigned per user; quota key feature reports per-key (per-tenant) independently; keyed_by_normalized_query_hash gives each query pattern own bucket
evidence.supports: Multi-tenant isolation: resource quotas for tenant-level throttling

evidence.snippet: Five multi-tenant patterns documented: shared table with tenant_id + row policies (recommended), separate tables, separate databases, compute-compute separation via Warehouses, separate cloud service; RBAC via GRANT statements and row policies with SQL examples
evidence.supports: Multi-tenant isolation patterns with concrete SQL examples

evidence.snippet: ReplicatedMergeTree replicates data; ClickHouse Keeper required for coordination (ZooKeeper also possible); 3+ Keeper nodes recommended; if one host fails the other replica continues serving reads and accepts writes; failed node auto-syncs on restart
evidence.supports: Recovery: replication via ReplicatedMergeTree, Keeper dependency, node failure behavior

evidence.snippet: ClickHouse Keeper uses Raft; 3-node cluster tolerates 1 crash; quorum loss requires recovery mode via rcvr four-letter command or --force-recovery argument; isro command tests read-only state; linearizable writes but non-linearizable reads by default
evidence.supports: Recovery: Keeper quorum loss recovery procedure, read-only mode indicators

evidence.snippet: LICENSE file header: 'Copyright 2016-2026 ClickHouse, Inc.' followed by full text of 'Apache License Version 2.0, January 2004'
evidence.supports: License: ClickHouse OSS is Apache License 2.0, NOT GPL v2

evidence.snippet: Window functions supported with OVER, PARTITION BY, ORDER BY, ROWS/RANGE/GROUPS frames, aggregate functions over frames, rank/dense_rank/row_number/percent_rank/cume_dist/lag/lead/ntile; INTERVAL syntax for DateTime RANGE OFFSET unsupported
evidence.supports: Version caveat: window functions are mature and broadly supported in current versions

evidence.snippet: 2026 OSS changelog: GROUPS frame mode for window functions (new feature); non-partitioned window functions experimental in distributed plans (make_distributed_plan); pipe operators in SQL; BigQuery engine; Keeper LSM tree storage; multi-stage distributed query execution via planner splitting into scatter/broadcast/gather/shuffle stages
evidence.supports: Version caveats 2026: GROUPS frame, non-partitioned window functions experimental in distributed plans, multi-stage execution

evidence.snippet: 2024 OSS changelog: QUALIFY clause (24.4); recursive CTEs (24.4); lightweight deletes partition support (24.9); refreshable materialized views production-ready (24.10); JSON data type experimental (24.8 LTS); analyzer promoted to production (24.8 LTS); parallel replicas beta (24.10); Dynamic type (24.5); BFloat16 (24.11)
evidence.supports: Version caveats 2024: materialized views, QUALIFY, analyzer, JSON type, parallel replicas

evidence.snippet: 2023 OSS changelog: lightweight delete capability introduced v23.1 (enabled via enable_lightweight_delete setting); refreshable materialized views implemented v23.12; window functions received parallel evaluation improvement v23.9 and NULL handling changes v23.11
evidence.supports: Version caveats 2023: lightweight deletes first introduced, refreshable MVs first appeared

evidence.snippet: Iceberg table engine provides read+write integration with Apache Iceberg tables on S3/Azure/HDFS/local; maps primitive and complex types; supports schema evolution, partition pruning, time travel; cannot write to decimal/fixed/timestamp_ns partition fields; cannot create or evolve schemas with Bool/Decimal/FixedString types; reads position and equality deletes but not v3 deletion vectors
evidence.supports: Lake interoperability: Iceberg read/write support with documented limitations

evidence.snippet: S3Queue engine for streaming import from S3 (similar to Kafka/RabbitMQ engines); modes unordered/ordered/exclusive; after_processing actions keep/delete/move/tag; persistent processing nodes since 25.8 prevent duplicates on keeper session expiry; duplicate rows possible from parsing errors or keeper session expiry
evidence.supports: Bulk/incremental load from object storage via S3Queue (introduced 23.8)

evidence.snippet: CDC pipeline: PostgreSQL WAL logical decoding via Debezium → Kafka → ClickHouse ReplacingMergeTree; version column tracks latest row state; deleted flag marks removal; queries need FINAL operator for correctness since dedup is eventual; ORDER BY columns must be immutable
evidence.supports: CDC pattern with PostgreSQL: Debezium→Kafka→ClickHouse with ReplacingMergeTree and versioning
